title: Cloud & DevOps
description: Understand cloud infrastructure, automate delivery, and operate services with observability, rollback, reliability, and cost awareness.

paths.title: Cloud Foundations
paths.description: Understand compute, storage, networking, regions, and shared responsibility.

paths.title: Build a Delivery Pipeline
paths.description: Move code through automated checks, artifacts, deployment, and rollback.

paths.title: Reliable Operations
paths.description: Use observability, scaling, backups, and cost controls.

cards.title: Cloud computing rents managed infrastructure and services
cards.prompt: Cloud platforms provide on-demand compute, storage, networking, databases, queues, and higher-level services.
cards.content: Cloud does not remove operational responsibility. It changes which responsibilities belong to the provider and which remain with the customer.

cards.title: Regions and zones limit failure scope
cards.prompt: A region is a geographic area; availability zones are isolated locations within a region.
cards.content: Deploying across zones can improve availability, while cross-region designs add cost, latency, and data-governance considerations.

cards.title: Choose object storage
cards.prompt: Which workload best fits object storage?

question.explanation: Object storage is designed for durable files and blobs accessed by key or URL.

cards.title: Infrastructure as code makes environments reproducible
cards.prompt: Infrastructure definitions describe resources in version-controlled files instead of relying on manual dashboard clicks.
cards.content: Reviewable changes, repeatable environments, and drift detection reduce configuration inconsistency.

cards.title: Design a basic CI pipeline
cards.prompt: Continuous integration checks each proposed change before it reaches production.
cards.content: Fast feedback encourages small changes and prevents known failures from being merged.
steps: Block merge when required checks fail.

cards.title: Build once, promote the same artifact
cards.prompt: The artifact tested in CI should be the artifact deployed to later environments.
cards.content: Rebuilding separately for production can introduce dependency or configuration differences that bypass earlier validation.

cards.title: Choose a safe rollout
cards.prompt: Which deployment strategy gradually exposes a new version to a small percentage of traffic?

question.explanation: A canary rollout limits initial exposure and allows metrics to guide continuation or rollback.

cards.title: Prepare rollback
cards.prompt: Rollback must be designed before the release fails.
cards.content: Database changes often need backward-compatible migration steps because application rollback alone may not reverse changed data.
items: Test rollback in a non-production environment.

cards.title: Observability connects metrics, logs, and traces
cards.prompt: Metrics show trends, logs provide event detail, and traces follow work across services.
cards.content: Useful telemetry is tied to user outcomes and service objectives, not only CPU and memory.

cards.title: Autoscaling does not fix every bottleneck
cards.prompt: Adding instances helps only when work can be distributed and dependencies can handle the extra load.
cards.content: Databases, queues, rate limits, cold starts, and shared locks can remain limiting factors.

cards.title: Measure user-facing reliability
cards.prompt: Which indicator most directly reflects whether users receive successful responses?

question.explanation: Successful request rate is a service-level indicator tied to user-visible outcomes.

cards.title: Operate a cloud service responsibly
cards.prompt: Reliability, security, and cost should be visible during normal operation.
cards.content: Assign owners and alerts to actionable conditions; noisy alerts train teams to ignore real incidents.
